## Why this unit matters

Start with a modular shop application. Follow the pressure to split deployments, then confront remote-call failure and learn which components address it.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Evolution of Application Architecture](architecture-evolution.qmd)**
2. **[Distributed Systems and CAP](distributed-systems-and-cap.qmd)**
3. **[Spring Cloud Ecosystem](spring-cloud-overview.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Source mapping and example

**Supplied source:** Day 1 §1–2. The content is an original explanation of the supplied course's topics and not a reproduction of its Java code. Start the [single-file Node.js shop lab](../examples/README.md) to inspect the related HTTP endpoints. Framework-specific components that are not present in the lab are explained as architectural patterns.
